title: User may be unaware that wearing the device continuously shares personal data
description: By wearing and using the device, the wearer shares continuous sensor telemetry including heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps with the wearable device. The wearer may not fully understand that this constitutes ongoing disclosure of sensitive personal data, especially location and health-related telemetry, or the extent and persistence of that collection.
assumptions: Assumes the device does not provide sufficiently clear, timely, and specific notice about continuous collection and sharing of telemetry.

title: User may lack meaningful consent for continuous telemetry capture
description: The flow involves continuous capture of multiple categories of personal data, including potentially sensitive health and location data. If the wearer has not given specific, informed, and freely given consent for this ongoing collection, the sharing from the user to the device may be non-compliant with applicable privacy requirements.
assumptions: Assumes consent is the relevant legal basis for at least some of the telemetry processing, particularly GPS and health-related data.
uncertainty_note: Tree node citation is based on best judgement because the retrieved context did not include the detailed non-compliance threat tree.

title: Telemetry in this flow can enable linkage of the wearer across time and contexts
description: The combination of heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps creates a rich behavioral pattern. Even within this single flow, these data points can be correlated over time to link multiple observations to the same wearer and reconstruct routines or repeated visits.
assumptions: Assumes telemetry is transmitted or represented in a form that preserves temporal and contextual continuity across observations.
uncertainty_note: Tree node citation is based on best judgement because the retrieved context did not include the detailed linkability threat tree.

title: Telemetry in transit can identify the wearer
description: GPS traces, timestamps, and distinctive activity or physiological patterns may directly or indirectly identify the wearer, even if explicit identifiers are absent. Home/work locations and repeated movement patterns are especially identifying.
assumptions: Assumes the telemetry is associated with a persistent device/session context or is sufficiently unique to single out an individual.
uncertainty_note: Tree node citation is based on best judgement because the retrieved context did not include the detailed identifiability threat tree.

title: The wearable device can infer sensitive information from received telemetry
description: Once the wearable device receives continuous heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps, it can derive additional private information such as health status, exercise habits, daily routines, places visited, sleep patterns, and potentially religious, political, or medical inferences from location history.
assumptions: Assumes the device software processes or stores telemetry in a way that enables profiling or inference beyond the raw values received.
uncertainty_note: Tree node citation is based on best judgement because the retrieved context did not include the detailed detectability/disclosure threat tree; this is intended as information disclosure/inference at the destination.

title: Excessive disclosure of detailed activity and location data to the companion app
description: The wearable device shares exercise sessions, GPS traces, device identifier, and timestamps with the companion app. If all raw batches are sent by default when only a subset is needed for core app functionality, the device causes avoidable disclosure of sensitive personal data, especially precise location and temporal patterns.
assumptions: Assumes the companion app does not strictly require full-fidelity GPS traces and all timestamps for every sync operation.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-effort based on LINDDUN Pro data-disclosure/minimality concepts; exact subnode may differ in the canonical tree.

title: Identification through device identifier and unique movement patterns in transit
description: The sync flow contains a device id plus GPS traces and timestamps. Even if direct account identifiers are absent, these data can identify a specific individual by linking the unique device id or distinctive home/work movement patterns to a real person.
assumptions: Assumes the flow is observable by an attacker or intermediary, or that identifiers are exposed within protocol metadata or payload.
uncertainty_note: Exact threat-tree subnode is inferred from general identifiability via direct and indirect identifiers.

title: Linkability of multiple sync batches and contexts
description: Repeated transmission of the same device id together with timestamps and sensor/GPS batches enables different sync events to be linked to the same wearer over time. This supports reconstruction of longitudinal behavior across sessions and contexts.

uncertainty_note: Subnode selection is approximate; threat applicability is strong because stable identifiers and repeated observations are explicit in the flow.

description: Even without reading full payload contents, the presence, timing, size, and frequency of sync batches can reveal that the user exercised, traveled, or was active at particular times. This makes otherwise private activities detectable from the communication itself.

uncertainty_note: Exact node id is best-effort; detectability from communication metadata is the core concern.
